name: Sogdian
notes: STUB — no grapheme inventory modelled. Sogdian, an Eastern Middle Iranian language of Sogdia (Samarkand, Panjakent, Bukhara, Fergana; modern Uzbekistan/Tajikistan), the main lingua franca of the Silk Road and one of the official languages of the First Turkic Khanate. It survives in a large corpus across THREE distinct script traditions — the native Sogdian alphabet (an Aramaic-derived abjad-cum-alphabet with several regional cursive variants, ISO 15924 'Sogd'/'Sogo'), the Manichaean script, and the Syriac (Christian, 'Nestorian') script — with no single standard transliteration scheme unifying all three the way Hoffmann's does for Avestan; scholarly transliterations vary by script tradition and by editor. Building a cited grapheme->IPA inventory here would mean picking one script/editor's convention and presenting it as THE orthography, which is not supportable from the sources consulted. Added as a stub so it resolves as an ancestry/contact node (parallel to the arc.json/x-clade stub pattern) rather than left as a dangling reference from Eastern Iranian and Middle Iranian ancestry chains.
